response.text:
Recent work supports testing which history events actually change recommendations. SIGIR 2024’s [ExUA](https://www.amazon.science/publications/explainable-uncertainty-attribution-for-sequential-recommendation) uses gradient saliency to identify uncertainty-inducing interactions; [2025 counterfactual research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03606) searches for minimal history edits that change recommendations. A [September 2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27201) reports strong faithfulness for Integrated Gradients and GradientSHAP, but does not evaluate GRU4Rec and uses a separately trained probe. These findings motivate diagnostics, without establishing their validity for this GRU.

Proposed audit: hold candidates fixed; compare edits to recent coherent events against equally sized edits to older or random events, matching position, popularity and title/description overlap where possible. Separately shuffle event order and replace lexically similar but contextually different items. Measure candidate-score margins, rank changes and attribution-guided deletion effects against random deletion. These are model-sensitivity tests, not proof of user intent. Attribute scores through GRU input embeddings; preserve signed contributions and check baseline sensitivity. [Adebayo et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03292) motivate parameter/data randomization controls; [2024 follow-up work](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.02383) cautions that randomization metrics themselves can be distorted by noise and similarity measures. Parameter-randomized copies can provide diagnostic controls without fitting another predictor.

Public text supports lexical-overlap audits only. Ownership, compatibility, mood and willingness to choose now remain unknown unless explicitly reported. Record rejection reasons directly when available; do not convert missing interactions into rejection labels. [2024 research](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v238/dai24b.html) shows that differing feedback-observation rates can bias learning even when objectives align with user welfare.
